# The build stage runs on real Node, with bun copied in for the install.
#
# `oven/bun` has no Node: `vinxi build` (a `#!/usr/bin/env node` script) ran on
# Bun there, which ignores NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size and climbed past
# 10 GB bundling Monaco and the GoRules editor. Docker Desktop's default VM is
# smaller than that, so the build died with "cannot allocate memory" — and,
# before that, with the client bundle half-written and the SSR build failing on
# the missing `.vite/manifest.json`. On Node the same build peaks far lower and
# the heap is a limit we can set. The runtime stage below stays on Bun.
FROM oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine AS bun
FROM node:22-alpine AS builder
COPY --from=bun /usr/local/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bun

WORKDIR /app

# The whole project before installing, rather than the manifests first.
#
# Copying manifests alone is the usual trick for cache reuse, and it is what
# this file used to do — `package.json`, `frontend/package.json`,
# `backend/package.json`, install. But the root manifest is a *workspace root*
# and it names `tests` as well, so an install that cannot see that directory
# fails outright with `Workspace not found "tests"`. `docker compose up --build`
# therefore failed on every generated project that kept its test suite, which is
# the default; the root Dockerfile had already learned this and copies the whole
# context for the same reason. A generated project is rewritten wholesale
# anyway, so there was little cache to preserve.
#
# `bun install` still resolves a lockfile when the project has committed one —
# the generator writes none, because it has no registry to resolve against.
COPY . .
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile; else bun install; fi

WORKDIR /app/frontend

# Empty on purpose. A base URL compiled into a client bundle is an address the
# image can never be run under any other name; empty means "same origin as the
# page", and this server forwards /api/* to the API itself (src/routes/api/$.ts),
# which is what keeps the session cookie same-origin. BACKEND_URL, set at run
# time, is where that forwarding goes.
ARG VITE_API_URL=
ARG VITE_APP_URL
# Where the dictionary's Electric shape requests go. Empty means same origin
# (/api/v1/shape through this server). Compose sets it to the API's own port:
# each shape is a long poll, there are several, and a browser allows six HTTP/1.1
# connections per origin — so through this origin they took every slot and every
# chunk, navigation and API call queued behind them (a 15 s navigation timeout,
# 10 s notification polls). A second origin is a second pool of six.
ARG VITE_ELECTRIC_PROXY_URL=
ENV VITE_API_URL=${VITE_API_URL}
ENV VITE_APP_URL=${VITE_APP_URL}
ENV VITE_ELECTRIC_PROXY_URL=${VITE_ELECTRIC_PROXY_URL}

# Raise this if the build reports "heap out of memory"; lower it on a small
# Docker VM. Docker Desktop: Settings > Resources > Memory.
ARG BUILD_HEAP_MB=8192
RUN NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=${BUILD_HEAP_MB} node ./node_modules/.bin/vinxi build

# Prune to production dependencies *here* rather than re-installing in the
# runtime stage, and for the same reason as above: the runtime stage carries no
# `tests` directory, so an install run there would fail on the workspace it
# cannot see.
WORKDIR /app
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile --production; \
    else bun install --production; fi

# ─── runtime ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine

WORKDIR /app
# PORT is what the server actually binds; without it Nitro picks 3000 and the
# port the compose file publishes has nothing behind it. BACKEND_URL is where
# /api/* is forwarded — compose points it at the backend service.
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT={{config.frontendPort}} \
    BACKEND_URL=http://backend:{{config.backendPort}}

# The pruned dependency tree, carried over rather than reinstalled. Both trees,
# not just the root one: Bun keeps a workspace's own dependencies under that
# workspace rather than hoisting everything.
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/frontend/node_modules ./frontend/node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json ./

# Copy frontend application
COPY --from=builder /app/frontend/.output ./frontend/.output
COPY --from=builder /app/frontend/package.json ./frontend/

EXPOSE {{config.frontendPort}}

CMD ["bun", "run", "frontend/.output/server/index.mjs"]

name: CI - {{project.name}}

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop]

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}-frontend

jobs:
  type-check:
    name: Type Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run TypeScript compiler
        run: bun run type-check

  test:
    name: Unit Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: bun run test

      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          files: ./coverage/coverage-final.json
          flags: frontend
          name: frontend-coverage

  e2e:
    name: E2E Tests (bun:test)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: {{project.name}}
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: ..

      - name: Migrate and seed
        run: bun run db:setup
        working-directory: ../backend
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/{{project.name}}

      # The runner starts the backend itself and waits for its health check.
      # Record volume is reduced from the 1000 default so CI stays under the
      # timeout; the bulk-seed code path is still exercised.
      - name: Run E2E suites
        run: bun run test
        working-directory: ../tests
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/{{project.name}}
          E2E_BASE_URL: http://localhost:{{config.backendPort}}
          E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY: 100
          E2E_USERS_TO_CREATE: 10
          E2E_RANDOM_WORKFLOW_OPS: 25

  build:
    name: Build Docker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [type-check, test, e2e]
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop')
    permissions:
      contents: read

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to deploy to'

        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options:
          - staging
          - production

  IMAGE_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}-frontend

jobs:
  deploy-staging:
    name: Deploy to Staging
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment:
      name: staging
      url: https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build application
        run: bun run build
        env:
          VITE_APP_URL: https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          VITE_API_URL: https://api-staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com

      - name: Deploy to Vercel (Staging)
        uses: vercel/action@master
        with:
          vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
          vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID_STAGING }}
          scope: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          env: VITE_APP_URL=https://staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,VITE_API_URL=https://api-staging-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com

      - name: Slack Notification
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0

          payload: |

              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "*{{project.name}} - Staging Deployment*\nStatus: ${{ job.status }}\nCommit: <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}|${{ github.sha }}>\nAuthor: ${{ github.actor }}"

    name: Deploy to Production
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.environment == 'production'
    environment:
      name: production
      url: https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com

      group: production

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Create GitHub Deployment
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        id: deployment
        with:
          script: |
            const deployment = await github.rest.repos.createDeployment({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              ref: context.ref,
              environment: 'production',
              required_contexts: [],
              auto_merge: false
            });
            return deployment.data.id;

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v1
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build application
        run: bun run build
        env:
          VITE_APP_URL: https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          VITE_API_URL: https://api-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com
          NODE_ENV: production

      - name: Deploy to Vercel (Production)
        uses: vercel/action@master
        with:
          vercel-token: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }}
          vercel-org-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}
          vercel-project-id: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_PROJECT_ID_PRODUCTION }}
          scope: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_ORG_ID }}

          env: VITE_APP_URL=https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,VITE_API_URL=https://api-{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com,NODE_ENV=production

      - name: Update GitHub Deployment Status
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        if: success()
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              deployment_id: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.result }},
              state: 'success',
              environment_url: 'https://{{project.id | slugify}}.example.com',
              description: 'Deployment succeeded'

      - name: Update GitHub Deployment Status (Failure)
        uses: actions/github-script@v6
        if: failure()
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.repos.createDeploymentStatus({
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              deployment_id: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.result }},
              state: 'failure',
              description: 'Deployment failed'
            });

      - name: Slack Notification
        if: always()
        uses: slackapi/slack-github-action@v1.24.0
        with:
          payload: |
            {
              "text": "Production deployment for {{project.name}}",
              "blocks": [
                {
                  "type": "section",
                  "text": {
                    "type": "mrkdwn",
                    "text": "*{{project.name}} - Production Deployment*\nStatus: ${{ job.status }}\nCommit: <${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/commit/${{ github.sha }}|${{ github.sha }}>\nAuthor: ${{ github.actor }}"
                  }
                }
              ]
            }
        env:
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
          SLACK_WEBHOOK_TYPE: INCOMING_WEBHOOK

  notify-completion:
    name: Notify Completion
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [deploy-staging]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "# Deployment Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "**Staging Status:** ${{ needs.deploy-staging.result }}" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

 * window from everyone but admin — a restriction on deleting quietly becoming a
 * restriction on looking.

 * `sys_access` answers "which windows may this role open", this answers "may
 * this role perform this operation on this table".

 * close a pair to the roles they name. That is what makes the directive
 * additive: a model declaring no `%%rbac` leaves every operation exactly as
 * open as it was before this table existed.

 * role *names* by the session guard, seeding is then order-independent, and a

FROM oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# The whole project before installing, rather than the manifests first.
#
# Copying manifests alone is the usual trick for cache reuse, and it is what
# this file used to do — `package.json`, `backend/package.json`,
# `frontend/package.json`, install. But the root manifest is a *workspace root*
# and it names `tests` as well, so an install that cannot see that directory
# fails outright with `Workspace not found "tests"`. `docker compose up --build`
# therefore failed on every generated project that kept its test suite, which is
# the default; the root Dockerfile had already learned this and copies the whole
# context for the same reason. A generated project is rewritten wholesale
# anyway, so there was little cache to preserve.
#
# `bun install` still resolves a lockfile when the project has committed one —
# the generator writes none, because it has no registry to resolve against.
COPY . .
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile; else bun install; fi

WORKDIR /app/backend
RUN bun run build

# Prune to production dependencies *here* rather than re-installing in the
# runtime stage, and for the same reason as above: the runtime stage carries no
# `tests` directory, so an install run there would fail on the workspace it
# cannot see.
WORKDIR /app
RUN if [ -f bun.lock ]; then bun install --frozen-lockfile --production; \
    else bun install --production; fi

# ─── runtime ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM oven/bun:1.4.4-alpine

WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# The pruned dependency tree, carried over rather than reinstalled. Both trees,
# not just the root one: Bun keeps a workspace's own dependencies under that
# workspace rather than hoisting everything, so copying only `/app/node_modules`
# yields an image whose application cannot resolve `pg`.
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/node_modules ./backend/node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json ./
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/package.json ./backend/

# Copy backend application. `src` and `seeds` travel as sources because the
# migrations and seeds are looked up by path at runtime rather than imported.
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/dist ./backend/dist
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/src ./backend/src
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/seeds ./backend/seeds
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/tsconfig.json ./backend/

# The model the application was generated from. The assistant reads it at
# `../model/model.eml.mmd` relative to the backend, and without it every
# start logs "No model/model.eml.mmd shipped with this application" and the
# model-context assistant answers nothing.
COPY --from=builder /app/model ./model

# Copy startup script
COPY --from=builder /app/backend/run-app.sh ./backend/
RUN chmod +x ./backend/run-app.sh

EXPOSE {{config.port}}

CMD ["/app/backend/run-app.sh"]

#!/bin/sh
# The backend container's entrypoint.
#
# It brings the schema up before it starts the API, and it is the only thing in
# the split build that does. `docker-start.sh` already did this for the
# single-image build; the compose file's `backend` service had no equivalent
# step, so `docker compose up` against a fresh volume started the API on an
# empty database and the process died on its first query —
# `relation "sys_system" does not exist` — leaving compose reporting nothing
# more useful than "container is unhealthy".
#
# `migrate` runs the migrations *and* the seeds, and both halves are safe to
# repeat: migrations are tracked by filename and the seeds swallow duplicate
# keys. So this runs on every start rather than only the first. Set
# SKIP_MIGRATE=true where something else owns the schema.
set -e

log() { echo "[backend] $*"; }

cd /app/backend

if [ -n "$DATABASE_URL" ] && [ "${SKIP_MIGRATE:-false}" != "true" ]; then
  # A handful of attempts, not an unbounded wait. Compose already orders this
  # behind `depends_on: postgres: service_healthy`, so the only thing left to
  # absorb is a database that accepts connections a moment before it will serve
  # them. Anything that survives the retries is a real failure — a bad
  # migration, a seed the model cannot satisfy — and looping on it would bury
  # the error in a wall of identical output instead of stopping on it.
  attempts=${DB_SETUP_ATTEMPTS:-5}
  n=1
  while :; do
    if bun run migrate; then
      break
    fi
    if [ "$n" -ge "$attempts" ]; then
      log "database setup failed after $n attempts — see the error above"
      exit 1
    fi
    log "database setup failed (attempt $n of $attempts) — retrying in 3s"
    n=$((n + 1))
    sleep 3
  done
fi

log "starting the API"
# Try node first (if available), fall back to bun
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  exec node -r tsconfig-paths/register /app/backend/dist/src/main.js
else
  export NODE_PATH=/app/node_modules:/app/backend/node_modules
  exec bun run /app/backend/dist/src/main.js
fi

# the proxy, and only the rows the caller's roles allow.
# ELECTRIC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3000

# Caches — how long each in-process cache serves an entry, in milliseconds.
#
# Every cache drops an entry the moment the application knows it changed (an
# access change is announced by the database to every instance); the expiry
# bounds how long an instance can be wrong when that signal is lost. 0 turns a
# cache off, so every read goes to the database — measure with it before tuning.
# Each one is logged at start-up (cache.configured) with the value in use.
CACHE_TTL_DEFAULT_MS=6000
# A user's access: which entities, operations and moves their roles grant (one query, sys_user_capability)
CACHE_TTL_CAPABILITIES_MS=6000
# Which entities, operations and moves are restricted at all — the same for every user
CACHE_TTL_ACCESS_POLICY_MS=6000
# Entity metadata: the dictionary's columns, fields and references for one entity
CACHE_TTL_ENTITY_METADATA_MS=6000
# The columns that name a record (its display value), per referenced table
CACHE_TTL_IDENTIFIER_FIELDS_MS=6000
# The dictionary's field lists served to the form and the grid
CACHE_TTL_DICTIONARY_FIELDS_MS=6000
# A record's lifecycle lookup: the moves out of a status and who may make them
CACHE_TTL_LIFECYCLE_MS=6000

# {{project.name}} — End-to-End Tests

Dependency-light end-to-end tests for the generated application. Everything here runs
on `node:test` — there is no Playwright, Jest or Vitest in this directory.

The suites drive the application through its **HTTP API**, the same surface the
generated frontend uses: they sign in with a real session cookie, exercise CRUD
for every entity, register business rules and prove they fire, and follow the
rule → workflow → cross-entity write chain.

---

## Running

```bash
# From the project root — generates nothing, just runs
npm run test:e2e
```

or from this directory:

```bash
npm install
npm run test          # everything, in order (starts the backend for you)
npm run test:fast     # skip the 1000-record bulk seed
npm run test:attach   # attach to a backend you already started
```

Target one group:

```bash
npm run test:crud
npm run test:rules
npm run test:workflows
npm run test:users
```

Or a single file:

```bash
node --test suites/01-auth.test.ts
```

### Prerequisites

The database must be migrated and seeded — the suites sign in as the seeded
administrator and assume the Application Dictionary is populated:

```bash
cd ../backend && npm run db:setup
```

The runner starts the backend itself unless one is already listening on the
configured port.

---

## Layout

```
tests/
├── run.ts              # Orchestrator — starts the app, runs suites in order
├── harness/            # Shared machinery, no tests
│   ├── config.ts       # Env-driven configuration
│   ├── http.ts         # fetch client + cookie jar (keeps the session)
│   ├── auth.ts         # login / register / permissions
│   ├── server.ts       # start + health-poll the backend
│   ├── entities.ts     # Entity registry generated from the ERD
│   ├── factory.ts      # Faker record factory
│   ├── rules.ts        # JDM builders + rules API
│   ├── workflows.ts    # Workflow run polling
│   └── harness.ts      # The controller: setup, tracking, teardown
└── suites/             # One file per functional area
    ├── 00-health.test.ts
    ├── 01-auth.test.ts
    ├── 02-dictionary.test.ts
    ├── 03-crud.<entity>.test.ts     (one per entity)
    ├── 04-bulk-seed.test.ts
    ├── 05-rules.<entity>.test.ts    (one per entity)
    ├── 06-rules-workflow.test.ts
    ├── 07-workflow-random.test.ts
    └── 08-users-roles.test.ts
```

Suites run in filename order because they build on each other: the bulk seed
populates the tables the rules and workflow suites then operate on.

---

## The harness

Every suite calls the same shared harness:

```ts
import { harness, getEntity, buildRecord } from "../harness/index.ts";

beforeAll(async () => { await harness.setup(); });   // wait for server + login
afterAll(async () => { await harness.teardown(); }); // delete what we created
```

`harness.setup()` is idempotent per process. `harness.createWithParents(entity)`
creates a record and, when the entity has foreign keys, creates or reuses the
parent records first — so a suite never has to know the shape of the ERD.

Anything created through the harness is tracked and removed on teardown, in
reverse order so children go before parents. The bulk-seed suite deliberately
opts out: its volume data is left behind for the suites that follow.

---

## What each suite covers

| Suite | Covers |
|-------|--------|
| `00-health` | Server reachable, health endpoint, protected routes reject anonymous callers |
| `01-auth` | Sign-in as the seeded admin, session persistence, bad credentials, registration, sign-out |
| `02-dictionary` | Every ERD column registered in `sys_column`; form and grid field ordering |
| `03-crud.<entity>` | List, create, read, update (PATCH + PUT), version bump, validation rejection, 404s, sort, search, filter, soft delete |
| `04-bulk-seed` | {{config.recordsPerEntity}}+ faker records per entity, parents first; totals and pagination at volume |
| `05-rules.<entity>` | JDM built and validated, rule registered, valid records pass, invalid records prevented, dry-run has no side effects, deactivation stops enforcement |
| `06-rules-workflow` | `trigger-workflow` actions emitted and workflow runs enqueued, reaching a terminal state |
| `07-workflow-random` | Randomised creates/updates across random entities with cascade rules; no 5xx, no stuck runs, records stay readable |
| `08-users-roles` | Seeded roles, faker-registered users at volume, permission scoping, admin-only route enforcement |

---

## Configuration

Every knob is an environment variable — see `harness/config.ts`.

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `E2E_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:{{config.port}}` | Backend under test |
| `E2E_ORIGIN` | `http://localhost:{{config.frontendPort}}` | Origin header (CORS + better-auth) |
| `E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL` | `admin@admin.com` | Seeded administrator |
| `E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `administrator` | Seeded administrator password |
| `E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY` | `1000` | Bulk-seed volume per entity |
| `E2E_SEED_BATCH_SIZE` | `25` | Concurrent inserts per batch |
| `E2E_USERS_TO_CREATE` | `25` | Users registered by the users suite |
| `E2E_RANDOM_WORKFLOW_OPS` | `50` | Random operations in the chaos suite |
| `E2E_FAKER_SEED` | `20260731` | Fixed so failures reproduce exactly |
| `E2E_WORKFLOW_TIMEOUT_MS` | `20000` | How long to wait for a workflow run |
| `E2E_VERBOSE` | unset | `1` logs every HTTP request |

Lower the volume for a quick local run:

```bash
E2E_RECORDS_PER_ENTITY=25 npm run test
```

---

## Reproducing a failure

The faker seed is fixed, so a failing bulk or chaos run replays identically.
Re-run the single suite that failed with verbose logging:

```bash
E2E_VERBOSE=1 node --test suites/07-workflow-random.test.ts
```

To replay with a different data set, change `E2E_FAKER_SEED`.

# {{project.name}} — configuration for `docker compose up --build`
#
#   cp .env.example .env      # then edit, then: docker compose up --build
#
# Compose reads `.env` from this directory automatically. Every value below has
# a working default baked into docker-compose.yml, so an empty `.env` still
# brings the application up — this file exists for the two things that have no
# sensible default: your own secrets, and where your AI endpoint lives.

# ── Secrets ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Change these before this runs anywhere but your laptop. The compose defaults
# are the literal string "change-me-in-production", which is a reminder, not a
# secret.
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=change-me-in-production-use-a-long-random-string
JWT_SECRET=change-me-in-production
SESSION_SECRET=change-me-in-production

# Database credentials for the bundled Postgres container.
DB_USER=app
DB_PASSWORD=app

# ── The AI assistant ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The application ships one AI feature: a retrieval assistant that answers
# questions about this application's own model. It works by **embedding** the
# model document into pgvector, so what it needs is an endpoint that serves
# OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/embeddings`.
#
# That is the whole contract. Anything speaking it works — pick one of the
# three below, uncomment it, and leave the others commented.
#
# 1) A LOCAL MODEL — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM, text-embeddings-inference.
#    `host.docker.internal` is how a container reaches a server on your machine;
#    on Linux add `--add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway` or use the
#    host's LAN address.
#
AI_BASE_URL=http://host.docker.internal:8000/v1
AI_API_KEY=local
AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL=bge-small-en-v1.5
AI_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=384

# 2) OPENAI — hosted, no local model to run.
#    Mind AI_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS: it is the pgvector column width and is fixed
#    when the index is created. Changing it later means re-creating the index
#    and re-ingesting, so set it before the first start.
#
# AI_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1
# AI_API_KEY=sk-...
# AI_EMBEDDING_MODEL=text-embedding-3-small
# AI_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS=1536
#
# 3) ANTHROPIC (Claude) — read this before reaching for a key.
#    The Claude API has no embeddings endpoint, and it is not OpenAI-shaped:
#    it is `POST /v1/messages` with `x-api-key` and `anthropic-version` headers,
#    not `POST /v1/embeddings` with a bearer token. So a Claude key cannot serve
#    the assistant on its own — there is nothing for it to answer.
#    Pair it with an embeddings provider (option 1 or 2 above) and put the key
#    here; the application does not call it today, and this is where it will
#    read it from when a chat surface is added.
#
# ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

# Leave the assistant off entirely — the application is fully functional
# without it, and every other screen is unaffected.
# ENABLE_MODEL_CONTEXT=false

# ── Ports, if the defaults collide with something ────────────────────────────
# FRONTEND_PORT={{project.frontendPort}}
# BACKEND_PORT={{project.backendPort}}

# ── Reaching the app by a name other than localhost ───────────────────────────
# The API checks the sign-in request's Origin. Left unset on a non-localhost
# host, sign-in answers "Invalid origin".
# CORS_ORIGIN=http://app.internal:{{project.frontendPort}}

# ── The reporting application ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# `docker compose up` brings up a second application beside this one: the
# Enterprise Reporting platform, holding this application's schema as a data
# source and the reports, charts and dashboard derived from the same model.
# It has its own sign-in and its own accounts — see reporting/README.md, which
# names both sets.
#
# Set these before the first start. The defaults in docker-compose.yml are
# placeholders so that an absent .env still brings everything up.

# Where the reporting application is published.
# REPORT_PORT=3100

# Session signing. At least 32 characters.
#   openssl rand -base64 32
# REPORT_AUTH_SECRET=

# What the platform encrypts the stored data-source password with. Exactly 64
# hex characters.
#   openssl rand -hex 32
#
# It has to stay the same once set: regenerating it leaves every stored
# connection undecryptable, and the failure looks like a broken data source
# rather than a rotated key.
# REPORT_ENCRYPTION_KEY=

# The platform version to build. Defaults to `main`, which is right while this
# project is something you are looking at and wrong once it is something you
# deploy — pin a commit then.
# REPORT_REF=main
